title: T Flip-Flop: One Input, One Toggle per Edge
topic: Toggle flip-flop — when T=1, Q flips on every rising clock edge; when T=0, Q holds. The frequency-divide-by-two building block of every binary counter.

beats.narration: What if a flip-flop had just one rule — flip on every tick?

elements.content: One input, one rule — Q flips on every rising edge.

beats.narration: Here's a T flip-flop. T on top — the toggle enable. Clock on the bottom with the edge-trigger triangle. Q on the output side.

elements.content: Rectangular FF block with T input on top, CLK input with triangle on bottom, Q output on right
T, CLK, Q labels with edge-trigger triangle on CLK
two rows: T=0 → Q holds, T=1 → Q toggles

beats.narration: The truth table has two rows. With T at zero, Q stays put. With T at one, Q becomes the inverse of its previous value on every clock edge.
Watch what happens with T held high. Every time the clock ticks up, Q flips. The output frequency is exactly half the clock — one T flip-flop is a divide-by-two.

elements.content: Three timing rows: CLK, T (held high), Q (toggles)
CLK square wave traces left to right, T constant high, Q toggles on each rising CLK edge
Cursor sweeps with toggle-pulses lighting up at each rising edge
f_out = f_clk / 2 — one T flip-flop divides the clock in half

beats.narration: Stack three T flip-flops with each one's Q driving the next one's clock — the ripple counter. Eight binary states from three toggling bits.

elements.content: Chain N of them → divide-by-2^N → binary counter
